content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, and built a full source ledger claim-by-claim and numeral-by-numeral.

**Ledger result:** every claim limitation, description statement, and figure-brief structure traces to an affirmative passage in `input/disclosure.md` (the disclosure text is reproduced verbatim as the first USER turn in `input/conversation.md`). The reversible two-screw fence, the keyed anti-rotation carriages, the shank-through-slot/clamping-shoe geometry, the parallel perpendicular bores, the per-carriage pointers and difference-equals-spacing result, the midpoint transverse center index, the shallow V-shaped sight notch, the parallel-faced spacer plate and its setback-only effect, the hardened-metal replaceable bushings, the rigid-polymer-or-metal part list, and the no-motor/battery/sensor/network negative limitation are all expressly disclosed. The schematic blocks, plain rectangular fence body, round knob bodies, graduation-line marks, break line, and hatching conventions stay confined to the figure briefs, are called "shown schematically," and add no undisclosed proportion, count, taper, depth, or contact topology; the application text never justifies them with "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language.

**Defects found are internal-consistency failures clustered on FIG. 3.** The Detailed Description calls FIG. 3 "a cross-sectional view taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 2," while the Brief Description and the FIG. 3 brief make it a fragmentary top plan view, and no 3-3 cutting-plane line exists in FIG. 2. That mislabel drags four downstream cross-reference errors with it, including reference numerals 72 and 80 that appear in the description and the ledger but on no drawing.

findings.title: FIG. 3 is given two incompatible identities and cites a section line 3-3 that exists in no drawing
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md (paragraph beginning "The construction of the guide carriages is shown in FIG. 3"); draft/07-drawings.md; figures/FIG-3.md; figures/FIG-2.md
findings.detail: The Detailed Description states: "The construction of the guide carriages is shown in FIG. 3, a cross-sectional view taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 2 through the second guide carriage 70, and in FIG. 5, a cross-sectional view taken on line 5-5 of FIG. 2 through the first guide carriage 50." The Brief Description says instead: "FIG. 3 is a fragmentary top plan view of the first and second guide carriages, showing the pointers," and the FIG. 3 brief is likewise "A fragmentary top plan view of the first and second guide carriages, showing the pointers." A top plan view cannot show the key 72 in the slot or the clamping shoe 80 below the rail, both of which the description attributes to FIG. 3. Moreover, the named section line 3-3 appears in no source-view brief: FIG. 2's brief recites only "A broken, offset cutting-plane line 5-5 establishes the cross-sectional view of FIG. 5," and the numeral list for FIG. 2 contains no 3 designation. The named section line therefore fails the requirement that the same designation appear in the source view, the resulting view, and the drawing description.
findings.evidence: Description: "The construction of the guide carriages is shown in FIG. 3, a cross-sectional view taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 2 through the second guide carriage 70". Brief Description: "FIG. 3 is a fragmentary top plan view of the first and second guide carriages, showing the pointers." FIG. 2 brief: "A broken, offset cutting-plane line 5-5 establishes the cross-sectional view of FIG. 5." (no 3-3 line anywhere).
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md replace the sentence "The construction of the guide carriages is shown in FIG. 3, a cross-sectional view taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 2 through the second guide carriage 70, and in FIG. 5, a cross-sectional view taken on line 5-5 of FIG. 2 through the first guide carriage 50. The two guide carriages are of the same construction." with "The construction of the guide carriages is shown in FIG. 5, a cross-sectional view taken on line 5-5 of FIG. 2 through the first guide carriage 50. The second guide carriage 70 is of the same construction as the first guide carriage 50." Make no change to FIG. 2, FIG. 3, or the Brief Description, so that line 5-5 remains the only named section line and carries the same designation in FIG. 2, in FIG. 5, and in the Brief Description.

findings.title: Reference numerals 72 and 80 are used in the description and ledger but appear on no figure
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md (guide-carriage construction and clamping paragraphs); draft/numerals.md rows for 72 and 80; figures/FIG-1.md through FIG-7.md numeral lists
findings.detail: The description recites "the second guide carriage 70 has a like key 72 (FIG. 3)", "the key 72 does the same for the second guide carriage 70", and "a clamping shoe 80 (FIG. 3) in the case of the second guide carriage 70", and draft/numerals.md lists "72 | key of the second guide carriage" and "80 | clamping shoe of the second guide carriage". No figure brief lists numeral 72 or numeral 80. FIG. 3's numeral list is 10, 18, 50, 54, 62, 70, 74, 82; FIG. 5's list is 10, 12, 16, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60. A reference character used in the description must appear in the drawings, and once FIG. 3 is correctly treated as a top plan view neither the key nor the shoe of the second carriage can be shown there.
findings.evidence: Description: "The first guide carriage 50 has a key 52 (FIG. 5) and the second guide carriage 70 has a like key 72 (FIG. 3)." and "a clamping shoe 60 (FIG. 5) in the case of the first guide carriage 50 and a clamping shoe 80 (FIG. 3) in the case of the second guide carriage 70." FIG. 3 numeral list: "10, 18, 50, 54, 62, 70, 74, 82" - no 72, no 80.
findings.fix: Delete the rows "| 72 | key of the second guide carriage |" and "| 80 | clamping shoe of the second guide carriage |" from draft/numerals.md, and in draft/08-detailed-description.md replace "The first guide carriage 50 has a key 52 (FIG. 5) and the second guide carriage 70 has a like key 72 (FIG. 3). The key 52 prevents rotation of the first guide carriage 50 relative to the rail 10 while permitting the first guide carriage 50 to slide along the longitudinal slot 16, and the key 72 does the same for the second guide carriage 70." with "The first guide carriage 50 has a key 52 (FIG. 5) and the second guide carriage 70 has a like key. The key 52 prevents rotation of the first guide carriage 50 relative to the rail 10 while permitting the first guide carriage 50 to slide along the longitudinal slot 16, and the like key of the second guide carriage 70 does the same for the second guide carriage 70." Correspondingly replace "is received in a clamping shoe below the rail 10, a clamping shoe 60 (FIG. 5) in the case of the first guide carriage 50 and a clamping shoe 80 (FIG. 3) in the case of the second guide carriage 70." with "is received in a clamping shoe below the rail 10, a clamping shoe 60 (FIG. 5) in the case of the first guide carriage 50 and a like clamping shoe in the case of the second guide carriage 70.", and replace the later sentence "The clamping shoe 60 and the clamping shoe 80 are each disposed below the lower face 14 of the rail 10 and bear against the lower face 14 when the clamp knob 58 and the clamp knob 78 respectively are tightened, and each is released from the lower face 14 when the clamp knob of its guide carriage is loosened." with "The clamping shoe of each guide carriage is disposed below the lower face 14 of the rail 10 and bears against the lower face 14 when the clamp knob of that guide carriage is tightened, and is released from the lower face 14 when that clamp knob is loosened." Also replace, in the materials paragraph, "the clamping shoe 60 and the clamping shoe 80," with "the clamping shoe 60 and the clamping shoe of the second guide carriage 70,".

findings.title: Upper face 12 is cross-referenced to FIG. 3, which does not label it
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, second paragraph ("Referring to FIG. 1, the drilling jig includes an elongated straight rail 10."); figures/FIG-3.md numeral list; figures/FIG-5.md numeral list
findings.detail: The description introduces the upper face with the parenthetical "(FIG. 3)", but FIG. 3's numeral list is "10, 18, 50, 54, 62, 70, 74, 82" and contains no numeral 12, and the FIG. 3 brief never mentions an upper face. Numeral 12 is labeled only in FIG. 5, whose brief states "The rail has an upper face 12" and whose numeral list includes 12. The cross-reference sends the examiner and the reader to a view in which the numeral does not appear.
findings.evidence: Description: "The rail 10 has a flat lower face 14 (FIG. 4) that rests on the front face of a workpiece 90, and an opposite upper face 12 (FIG. 3)." FIG. 3 numeral list: "10, 18, 50, 54, 62, 70, 74, 82". FIG. 5 brief: "The rail has an upper face 12."
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md change "and an opposite upper face 12 (FIG. 3)" to "and an opposite upper face 12 (FIG. 5)".

findings.title: First pointer 62 and second pointer 82 are said to be seen in FIG. 2, which does not show them
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md (pointer paragraph); figures/FIG-2.md numeral list; figures/FIG-3.md
findings.detail: The description states that the pointers are "as seen in FIG. 2", but FIG. 2's numeral list is "10, 16, 18, 30, 50, 58, 70, 78" and its brief never mentions a pointer. The pointers are shown only in FIG. 3, whose brief states "The first pointer 62 on the first guide carriage 50 and the second pointer 82 on the second guide carriage 70 are shown aligned with the distance marks 18" and whose numeral list includes 62 and 82. The Brief Description also assigns the pointers to FIG. 3 ("FIG. 3 is a fragmentary top plan view of the first and second guide carriages, showing the pointers"), so the description contradicts both the Brief Description and the figure brief.
findings.evidence: Description: "The first guide carriage 50 carries a first pointer 62 and the second guide carriage 70 carries a second pointer 82, as seen in FIG. 2." FIG. 2 numeral list: "10, 16, 18, 30, 50, 58, 70, 78" - no 62, no 82.
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md change "The first guide carriage 50 carries a first pointer 62 and the second guide carriage 70 carries a second pointer 82, as seen in FIG. 2." to "The first guide carriage 50 carries a first pointer 62 and the second guide carriage 70 carries a second pointer 82, as seen in FIG. 3."

findings.title: Clamp knob 78 is cross-referenced to FIGS. 1 and 3, but is labeled only in FIG. 2
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md (clamp knob paragraph); figures/FIG-1.md numeral list; figures/FIG-2.md numeral list; figures/FIG-3.md numeral list
findings.detail: The description recites "a clamp knob 78 (FIGS. 1 and 3) on the second guide carriage 70". FIG. 1's numeral list is "10, 30, 32, 50, 58, 70, 90, 92" and does not include 78, even though the FIG. 1 brief describes "a like clamp knob" over the second carriage without assigning it a numeral. FIG. 3's numeral list is likewise free of 78. The only figure that labels 78 is FIG. 2, whose brief states "The clamp knob 58 of the first guide carriage 50 and the clamp knob 78 of the second guide carriage 70 are shown" and whose numeral list includes 78.
findings.evidence: Description: "a clamp knob 58 (FIGS. 1 and 5) on the first guide carriage 50 and a clamp knob 78 (FIGS. 1 and 3) on the second guide carriage 70." FIG. 1 numeral list: "10, 30, 32, 50, 58, 70, 90, 92". FIG. 2 brief: "The clamp knob 58 of the first guide carriage 50 and the clamp knob 78 of the second guide carriage 70 are shown."
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md change "a clamp knob 78 (FIGS. 1 and 3) on the second guide carriage 70" to "a clamp knob 78 (FIG. 2) on the second guide carriage 70".

findings.title: Detailed Description repeats an untraced characterization of alternative jigs outside the Background
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The reversible mounting of the fence 30 addresses a practical difficulty of edge-referenced hole location."
findings.detail: Two sentences of this paragraph characterize how other tools behave and how users err with them. The disclosure contains no affirmative statement about turning a whole tool over, about a marked face being placed against the panel, or about a second set of oppositely running marks being misread. The nearest source passage is limited to the benefit of the invention: "This lets the same marked upper face be used when the tool is referenced from either an upper edge or a lower edge of a workpiece." The material is a prior-art characterization, which is unobjectionable in the Background (where it already appears in substantially identical form in the fourth Background paragraph) but is not inventor-supported invention matter when repeated in the Detailed Description.
findings.evidence: Description: "If the projecting part of an edge fence is permanently fixed to one longitudinal side of a marked rail, referencing the opposite edge requires either turning the whole tool over, which places the marked face against the panel where it cannot be read, or providing a second set of marks that runs in the opposite direction, which the user may read in error." Nearest source: "This lets the same marked upper face be used when the tool is referenced from either an upper edge or a lower edge of a workpiece." Background already states the same point: "A jig whose edge fence projects from one longitudinal side of its body can be referenced from the opposite edge only by turning the whole jig over..."
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md delete the two sentences "A pull on one cabinet component is commonly located from an upper edge of the component, while a pull on another component of the same run is commonly located from a lower edge. If the projecting part of an edge fence is permanently fixed to one longitudinal side of a marked rail, referencing the opposite edge requires either turning the whole tool over, which places the marked face against the panel where it cannot be read, or providing a second set of marks that runs in the opposite direction, which the user may read in error.", leaving the paragraph to read: "The reversible mounting of the fence 30 addresses a practical difficulty of edge-referenced hole location. Reversing the fence 30 alone moves the downwardly projecting portion 32 to the other longitudinal side of the rail 10 while leaving the rail 10, the distance marks 18, and the carriage settings undisturbed."

input.summary: Full source ledger built and traced: every limitation of all 22 claims (independent claims 1, 13, and 18 plus dependent claims 2-12, 14-17, and 19-22), every one of the 27 numerals in draft/numerals.md, every numbered part and structural, positional, material, and operational statement in the Summary, Detailed Description, Abstract, and all seven figure briefs was checked against affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md and the inventor's own first turn in input/conversation.md. Every technical item traces to an exact affirmative source passage: the elongated straight rail with flat lower face, upper face, and through-running straight longitudinal slot; printed distance marks beside the slot; the fixed, reversible fence secured at the first end by two screws in two corresponding holes with its downwardly projecting portion movable from one longitudinal side to the opposite side while the same marked upper face is used; the removable parallel-faced spacer plate that changes setback by its thickness without changing hole separation; two separate keyed guide carriages whose keys prevent rotation while permitting sliding; one cylindrical drill bushing per carriage with a bore passing completely through the carriage and registering with the slot; the two bores parallel to one another and perpendicular to the flat lower face; the threaded clamp knob whose shank passes through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail, clamping the rail between carriage and shoe; per-carriage pointers aligned with their bore axes and readable against the distance marks with the difference equal to center-to-center spacing; the transverse center index at the midpoint; the shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index and with a pencil centerline; the full method sequence ending with the jig lifted away and no part remaining attached; hardened-metal replaceable bushings; the rigid-polymer-or-metal part list; and the no-motor, no-battery, no-sensor, no-network negative limitation. No unsupported optional embodiment, variant, operating condition, or dependent-claim limitation was found; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, or unresolved alternative remains; no numeral carries two meanings; and Background prior-art characterizations were not treated as requiring inventor support. Figure-brief depiction choices (schematic blocks for carriages, round knob bodies, a plain rectangular fence body, graduation-line distance marks, the ragged break line, and hatching direction) stay confined to the figure briefs, are expressly called schematic, keep the claims and description shape-neutral, and add no untraced proportion, count, depth, taper, runout, angle, or contact topology; the application text nowhere justifies a renderer choice with "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language. The defects reported are internal-consistency failures, not source-fidelity gaps, and they cluster on FIG. 3: the Detailed Description calls FIG. 3 a cross-sectional view taken on a line 3-3 of FIG. 2 while the Brief Description and the FIG. 3 brief make it a fragmentary top plan view, and no 3-3 cutting-plane line appears in FIG. 2, whose only named section line is 5-5 (which is consistently designated in FIG. 2, FIG. 5, and the Brief Description). That mislabel produces four downstream figure-citation errors: numerals 72 (key of the second guide carriage) and 80 (clamping shoe of the second guide carriage) are used in the description and listed in the ledger but appear on no figure; upper face 12 is cited to FIG. 3 though only FIG. 5 labels it; pointers 62 and 82 are said to be seen in FIG. 2 though only FIG. 3 shows them; and clamp knob 78 is cited to FIGS. 1 and 3 though only FIG. 2 labels it. One minor item is a prior-art characterization of alternative jigs repeated inside the Detailed Description. Each finding carries a concrete quoted evidence pair and a filing-clean automatic fix.

findings.title: FIG. 3 is given two incompatible identities and cites a section line 3-3 that exists in no drawing
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md (paragraph beginning "The construction of the guide carriages is shown in FIG. 3"); draft/07-drawings.md; figures/FIG-3.md; figures/FIG-2.md
findings.detail: The Detailed Description states: "The construction of the guide carriages is shown in FIG. 3, a cross-sectional view taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 2 through the second guide carriage 70, and in FIG. 5, a cross-sectional view taken on line 5-5 of FIG. 2 through the first guide carriage 50." The Brief Description says instead: "FIG. 3 is a fragmentary top plan view of the first and second guide carriages, showing the pointers," and the FIG. 3 brief is likewise "A fragmentary top plan view of the first and second guide carriages, showing the pointers." A top plan view cannot show the key 72 in the slot or the clamping shoe 80 below the rail, both of which the description attributes to FIG. 3. Moreover, the named section line 3-3 appears in no source-view brief: FIG. 2's brief recites only "A broken, offset cutting-plane line 5-5 establishes the cross-sectional view of FIG. 5," and the numeral list for FIG. 2 contains no 3 designation. The named section line therefore fails the requirement that the same designation appear in the source view, the resulting view, and the drawing description.
findings.evidence: Description: "The construction of the guide carriages is shown in FIG. 3, a cross-sectional view taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 2 through the second guide carriage 70". Brief Description: "FIG. 3 is a fragmentary top plan view of the first and second guide carriages, showing the pointers." FIG. 2 brief: "A broken, offset cutting-plane line 5-5 establishes the cross-sectional view of FIG. 5." (no 3-3 line anywhere).
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md replace the sentence "The construction of the guide carriages is shown in FIG. 3, a cross-sectional view taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 2 through the second guide carriage 70, and in FIG. 5, a cross-sectional view taken on line 5-5 of FIG. 2 through the first guide carriage 50. The two guide carriages are of the same construction." with "The construction of the guide carriages is shown in FIG. 5, a cross-sectional view taken on line 5-5 of FIG. 2 through the first guide carriage 50. The second guide carriage 70 is of the same construction as the first guide carriage 50." Make no change to FIG. 2, FIG. 3, or the Brief Description, so that line 5-5 remains the only named section line and carries the same designation in FIG. 2, in FIG. 5, and in the Brief Description.

findings.title: Reference numerals 72 and 80 are used in the description and ledger but appear on no figure
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md (guide-carriage construction and clamping paragraphs); draft/numerals.md rows for 72 and 80; figures/FIG-1.md through FIG-7.md numeral lists
findings.detail: The description recites "the second guide carriage 70 has a like key 72 (FIG. 3)", "the key 72 does the same for the second guide carriage 70", and "a clamping shoe 80 (FIG. 3) in the case of the second guide carriage 70", and draft/numerals.md lists "72 | key of the second guide carriage" and "80 | clamping shoe of the second guide carriage". No figure brief lists numeral 72 or numeral 80. FIG. 3's numeral list is 10, 18, 50, 54, 62, 70, 74, 82; FIG. 5's list is 10, 12, 16, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60. A reference character used in the description must appear in the drawings, and once FIG. 3 is correctly treated as a top plan view neither the key nor the shoe of the second carriage can be shown there.
findings.evidence: Description: "The first guide carriage 50 has a key 52 (FIG. 5) and the second guide carriage 70 has a like key 72 (FIG. 3)." and "a clamping shoe 60 (FIG. 5) in the case of the first guide carriage 50 and a clamping shoe 80 (FIG. 3) in the case of the second guide carriage 70." FIG. 3 numeral list: "10, 18, 50, 54, 62, 70, 74, 82" - no 72, no 80.
findings.fix: Delete the rows "| 72 | key of the second guide carriage |" and "| 80 | clamping shoe of the second guide carriage |" from draft/numerals.md, and in draft/08-detailed-description.md replace "The first guide carriage 50 has a key 52 (FIG. 5) and the second guide carriage 70 has a like key 72 (FIG. 3). The key 52 prevents rotation of the first guide carriage 50 relative to the rail 10 while permitting the first guide carriage 50 to slide along the longitudinal slot 16, and the key 72 does the same for the second guide carriage 70." with "The first guide carriage 50 has a key 52 (FIG. 5) and the second guide carriage 70 has a like key. The key 52 prevents rotation of the first guide carriage 50 relative to the rail 10 while permitting the first guide carriage 50 to slide along the longitudinal slot 16, and the like key of the second guide carriage 70 does the same for the second guide carriage 70." Correspondingly replace "is received in a clamping shoe below the rail 10, a clamping shoe 60 (FIG. 5) in the case of the first guide carriage 50 and a clamping shoe 80 (FIG. 3) in the case of the second guide carriage 70." with "is received in a clamping shoe below the rail 10, a clamping shoe 60 (FIG. 5) in the case of the first guide carriage 50 and a like clamping shoe in the case of the second guide carriage 70.", and replace the later sentence "The clamping shoe 60 and the clamping shoe 80 are each disposed below the lower face 14 of the rail 10 and bear against the lower face 14 when the clamp knob 58 and the clamp knob 78 respectively are tightened, and each is released from the lower face 14 when the clamp knob of its guide carriage is loosened." with "The clamping shoe of each guide carriage is disposed below the lower face 14 of the rail 10 and bears against the lower face 14 when the clamp knob of that guide carriage is tightened, and is released from the lower face 14 when that clamp knob is loosened." Also replace, in the materials paragraph, "the clamping shoe 60 and the clamping shoe 80," with "the clamping shoe 60 and the clamping shoe of the second guide carriage 70,".

findings.title: Upper face 12 is cross-referenced to FIG. 3, which does not label it
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, second paragraph ("Referring to FIG. 1, the drilling jig includes an elongated straight rail 10."); figures/FIG-3.md numeral list; figures/FIG-5.md numeral list
findings.detail: The description introduces the upper face with the parenthetical "(FIG. 3)", but FIG. 3's numeral list is "10, 18, 50, 54, 62, 70, 74, 82" and contains no numeral 12, and the FIG. 3 brief never mentions an upper face. Numeral 12 is labeled only in FIG. 5, whose brief states "The rail has an upper face 12" and whose numeral list includes 12. The cross-reference sends the examiner and the reader to a view in which the numeral does not appear.
findings.evidence: Description: "The rail 10 has a flat lower face 14 (FIG. 4) that rests on the front face of a workpiece 90, and an opposite upper face 12 (FIG. 3)." FIG. 3 numeral list: "10, 18, 50, 54, 62, 70, 74, 82". FIG. 5 brief: "The rail has an upper face 12."
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md change "and an opposite upper face 12 (FIG. 3)" to "and an opposite upper face 12 (FIG. 5)".

findings.title: First pointer 62 and second pointer 82 are said to be seen in FIG. 2, which does not show them
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md (pointer paragraph); figures/FIG-2.md numeral list; figures/FIG-3.md
findings.detail: The description states that the pointers are "as seen in FIG. 2", but FIG. 2's numeral list is "10, 16, 18, 30, 50, 58, 70, 78" and its brief never mentions a pointer. The pointers are shown only in FIG. 3, whose brief states "The first pointer 62 on the first guide carriage 50 and the second pointer 82 on the second guide carriage 70 are shown aligned with the distance marks 18" and whose numeral list includes 62 and 82. The Brief Description also assigns the pointers to FIG. 3 ("FIG. 3 is a fragmentary top plan view of the first and second guide carriages, showing the pointers"), so the description contradicts both the Brief Description and the figure brief.
findings.evidence: Description: "The first guide carriage 50 carries a first pointer 62 and the second guide carriage 70 carries a second pointer 82, as seen in FIG. 2." FIG. 2 numeral list: "10, 16, 18, 30, 50, 58, 70, 78" - no 62, no 82.
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md change "The first guide carriage 50 carries a first pointer 62 and the second guide carriage 70 carries a second pointer 82, as seen in FIG. 2." to "The first guide carriage 50 carries a first pointer 62 and the second guide carriage 70 carries a second pointer 82, as seen in FIG. 3."

findings.title: Clamp knob 78 is cross-referenced to FIGS. 1 and 3, but is labeled only in FIG. 2
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md (clamp knob paragraph); figures/FIG-1.md numeral list; figures/FIG-2.md numeral list; figures/FIG-3.md numeral list
findings.detail: The description recites "a clamp knob 78 (FIGS. 1 and 3) on the second guide carriage 70". The only figure that labels 78 is FIG. 2, whose brief states "The clamp knob 58 of the first guide carriage 50 and the clamp knob 78 of the second guide carriage 70 are shown" and whose numeral list includes 78.

FIG. 1 numeral list: "10, 30, 32, 50, 58, 70, 90, 92". FIG. 2 brief: "The clamp knob 58 of the first guide carriage 50 and the clamp knob 78 of the second guide carriage 70 are shown."
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md change "a clamp knob 78 (FIGS. 1 and 3) on the second guide carriage 70" to "a clamp knob 78 (FIG. 2) on the second guide carriage 70".

findings.title: Detailed Description repeats an untraced characterization of alternative jigs outside the Background
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The reversible mounting of the fence 30 addresses a practical difficulty of edge-referenced hole location."
findings.detail: Two sentences of this paragraph characterize how other tools behave and how users err with them. The disclosure contains no affirmative statement about turning a whole tool over, about a marked face being placed against the panel, or about a second set of oppositely running marks being misread. The nearest source passage is limited to the benefit of the invention: "This lets the same marked upper face be used when the tool is referenced from either an upper edge or a lower edge of a workpiece." The material is a prior-art characterization, which is unobjectionable in the Background (where it already appears in substantially identical form in the fourth Background paragraph) but is not inventor-supported invention matter when repeated in the Detailed Description.
findings.evidence: Description: "If the projecting part of an edge fence is permanently fixed to one longitudinal side of a marked rail, referencing the opposite edge requires either turning the whole tool over, which places the marked face against the panel where it cannot be read, or providing a second set of marks that runs in the opposite direction, which the user may read in error." Nearest source: "This lets the same marked upper face be used when the tool is referenced from either an upper edge or a lower edge of a workpiece." Background already states the same point: "A jig whose edge fence projects from one longitudinal side of its body can be referenced from the opposite edge only by turning the whole jig over..."
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md delete the two sentences "A pull on one cabinet component is commonly located from an upper edge of the component, while a pull on another component of the same run is commonly located from a lower edge. If the projecting part of an edge fence is permanently fixed to one longitudinal side of a marked rail, referencing the opposite edge requires either turning the whole tool over, which places the marked face against the panel where it cannot be read, or providing a second set of marks that runs in the opposite direction, which the user may read in error.", leaving the paragraph to read: "The reversible mounting of the fence 30 addresses a practical difficulty of edge-referenced hole location. Reversing the fence 30 alone moves the downwardly projecting portion 32 to the other longitudinal side of the rail 10 while leaving the rail 10, the distance marks 18, and the carriage settings undisturbed."
